literal: At the time of ruin, the friendship of those who abandon, at the time of death, even if thought of, the mind will burn.
translation: The friendship of those who abandon you in times of ruin will burn your mind, even if you think of it at the moment of death.
modern: துன்பம் வரும் காலத்தில் கைவிட்டு விலகிப் போகின்றவர்களின் நட்பு, ஒருவருக்கு இறுதி காலம் நெருங்கும் போது நினைத்துப் பார்த்தாலும் மனதைச் சுட்டு வருத்தும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the lingering pain caused by fair-weather friends. The poet states that the friendship of those who abandon us when we fall into ruin (keṭuṅkālai) is so toxic that even thinking about it on one's deathbed (aṭuṅkālai) will burn the heart. The word 'aṭu' here means to destroy or kill, referring to the final moments of life. The betrayal of a false friend leaves a scar so deep that it hurts even at the very end of one's existence.
